synopsis: All six Codex debriefs completed and were well grounded: each correctly said the family's first committed choice was the non-recommended relocation and that it was blocked for lack of a confirmed destination, then pointed to arranging that destination with the recorded helper and, in five of six, to the essential device or medication continuity gap. No choice was invented, wording stayed in English, accessibility attributes followed recorded needs, and no internal IDs leaked. The main weakness is prioritization: both oak debriefs skipped the receipt's critical stored-water depletion (5 gallons against a 12-gallon target, empty by day two) even though a matching water task was supplied, and one lake debrief dropped the insulin continuity gap. One lake debrief added an unrecorded building-access topic.

fact_findings.finding: Omitted in oak 2/2; the two focus slots went to relocation and oxygen continuity. Defensible ordering, but the summary text never mentions water, which the receipt marks critical.
Lake 776f132a uses it (pharmacist instructions before buying cooling supplies); lake 98c4b8cd omits it.

Deterministic input defect: several receipt event titles for eq-oxygen and eq-insulin begin with an empty device name because the projection uses label rather than legacyOriginalLabel/purpose. Models compensated, but the native receipt rendering will show a blank subject.
